question: What is your age (in years)?
help_text: Informational. Biometrics apply to ages 14–79; police clearances matter from 18. Routes later questions.
mapped_rule: Biometrics Required for Most Applicants Aged 14–79
error_message: Enter your age in years. Biometrics apply to most applicants aged 14–79; this field is required to route your application correctly.

question: Which province/territory will you study in?
help_text: Province determines PAL vs TAL and whether Quebec's CAQ + higher Quebec funds apply.
mapped_rule: Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL) or Territorial Attestation Letter (TAL) Required
error_message: Select the province or territory where you will study. Your province determines whether you need a PAL or CAQ and affects the financial thresholds that apply.

question: Do you have a Letter of Acceptance (LOA) from a Designated Learning Institution (DLI)?
help_text: You cannot apply without an LOA from a DLI. An admission/offer email is not enough — you need the official LOA. Beware agents enrolling you at non-DLI 'colleges'.
mapped_rule: Must Be Enrolled at a Designated Learning Institution (DLI)
error_message: A valid Letter of Acceptance from a Designated Learning Institution (DLI) is mandatory. Your study permit application cannot proceed without one.

question: Have you personally verified your institution is on the official DLI list at canada.ca?
help_text: Check the DLI number on the government list yourself. Many Pakistani students are mis-sold into institutions that are not DLIs or have lost PGWP eligibility.
mapped_rule: Must Be Enrolled at a Designated Learning Institution (DLI)
error_message: You must personally verify your institution appears on the official DLI list at canada.ca. Agents sometimes direct students to unlisted or PGWP-ineligible institutions.

question: Do you have your institution's DLI number ready?
help_text: The DLI number (starts with 'O') is required in the application. It is on your LOA.
mapped_rule: Must Be Enrolled at a Designated Learning Institution (DLI)
error_message: Your DLI number (starting with 'O') must be entered in your study permit application. It is printed on your Letter of Acceptance.

question: Will you upload the LOA in the correct section of the application?
help_text: An LOA in the wrong field can cause the system not to register it. Follow the document checklist exactly.
mapped_rule: Letter of Acceptance (LOA) Required — Must Be Uploaded Correctly
error_message: Your LOA must be uploaded in the correct document section. An LOA placed in the wrong field may not be registered by IRCC.

question: Will your DLI confirm/validate your LOA with IRCC if asked?
help_text: Since the LOA-verification system, IRCC checks LOAs directly with institutions. A fake or unverifiable LOA = refusal and a misrepresentation finding.
mapped_rule: Letter of Acceptance (LOA) Required — Must Be Uploaded Correctly
error_message: IRCC verifies LOAs directly with institutions. A fake or unverifiable LOA results in refusal and a 5-year misrepresentation bar under A40.

question: Have you prepared a strong Letter of Explanation / Statement of Purpose?
help_text: Canada has no 'GS form' like Australia — your study plan/Letter of Explanation IS your case for being a genuine student who will leave on expiry. Weak SOPs and weak home ties are the top Pakistani refusal reasons.
mapped_rule: Bona Fide Student — Must Prove Intent to Leave Canada on Expiry
error_message: A Letter of Explanation (study plan/statement of purpose) is essential. Canada has no GS form — your LOE is your primary evidence of genuine study intent.

question: Which ties to Pakistan can you actually PROVE (not just claim)?
help_text: Officers weigh DOCUMENTABLE ties most: property in your name, a family business, a written return job offer. 'My parents live here' alone is weak.
mapped_rule: Bona Fide Student — Must Prove Intent to Leave Canada on Expiry
error_message: No documentable ties to Pakistan significantly weakens your bona fide student case. IRCC weighs concrete ties — property, business, employment — over verbal claims.

question: Can you give a specific, credible reason for THIS program at THIS school (not generic)?
help_text: Generic 'Canada has good education' reasoning gets refused. Tie the exact program/curriculum to your background and a Pakistan-based career outcome.
mapped_rule: Bona Fide Student — Must Prove Intent to Leave Canada on Expiry
error_message: A generic study rationale is a leading refusal cause. Name the specific program, connect it to your background, and link it to a Pakistan-based career outcome.

question: Can you justify choosing Canada over cheaper/closer options (local universities, Gulf, Malaysia)?
help_text: Officers probe whether study is the real purpose. Have a defensible reason tied to program quality/accreditation — not work or immigration.
mapped_rule: Bona Fide Student — Must Prove Intent to Leave Canada on Expiry
error_message: You should be able to justify choosing Canada over cheaper alternatives. Officers probe whether study is the genuine purpose of travel.

question: Does this program logically follow your past education/work, or can you justify a switch?
help_text: A drastic, unexplained downgrade or field-switch (e.g. completed Bachelors then a junior diploma) is a classic refusal trigger and signals non-genuine study.
mapped_rule: Bona Fide Student — Must Prove Intent to Leave Canada on Expiry
error_message: A drastic or unexplained field switch is a classic bona fide refusal trigger. Your Letter of Explanation must connect your previous qualification to this program.

question: Do you have documents (not just words) supporting your plan to return to Pakistan?
help_text: Attach what you can: property papers, family business registration, a conditional return offer. Dual intent is allowed, but you must still show you would leave if not granted PR.
mapped_rule: Bona Fide Student — Must Prove Intent to Leave Canada on Expiry
error_message: Documents supporting your plan to return to Pakistan strengthen your bona fide case. Attach property papers, business registration, or a conditional return offer where possible.

question: Are you applying to study in Quebec?
help_text: Quebec requires a CAQ (and higher funds from 2026). Non-Quebec provinces require a PAL/TAL instead. Routes the next questions.
mapped_rule: Quebec Applicants Need Certificat d'acceptation du Québec (CAQ)
error_message: Select whether you are applying to study in Quebec. Quebec applicants require a CAQ and face higher financial thresholds from 2026.

question: Are you a Masters/Doctoral student at a PUBLIC DLI (PAL/TAL-exempt from 2026)?
help_text: From 2026-01-01, Masters and doctoral students at public DLIs are exempt from the PAL/TAL requirement. If this is you, the PAL/TAL questions are not applicable.
mapped_rule: Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL) or Territorial Attestation Letter (TAL) Required
error_message: Masters and doctoral students at public DLIs are exempt from the PAL/TAL requirement from 2026-01-01. Indicate whether this exemption applies to you.

question: If required, do you have your Provincial/Territorial Attestation Letter (PAL/TAL)?
help_text: Most non-Quebec post-secondary applicants must include a PAL/TAL or the application is returned. It is issued by the province after you have an LOA.
mapped_rule: Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL) or Territorial Attestation Letter (TAL) Required
error_message: Most non-Quebec post-secondary applicants must submit a PAL/TAL with their application or it will be returned. It is issued by the province after you receive your LOA.

question: Will you submit the PAL/TAL WITH the application (not after)?
help_text: The PAL/TAL must be in the initial submission. Sending it later does not fix a returned application.
mapped_rule: Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL) or Territorial Attestation Letter (TAL) Required
error_message: The PAL/TAL must be included in your initial application submission. Sending it after the fact does not fix a returned application.

question: If studying in Quebec, do you have your CAQ?
help_text: Quebec study requires a CAQ from the province before/with the federal study permit. No CAQ = cannot proceed for Quebec.
mapped_rule: Quebec Applicants Need Certificat d'acceptation du Québec (CAQ)
error_message: Quebec study requires a Certificat d'acceptation du Québec (CAQ) from the province before the federal study permit can be issued. Without it the application cannot proceed.

question: Does your CAQ include the required attestation/allocation confirmation?
help_text: The CAQ must reflect Quebec's attestation/allocation. An incomplete CAQ will not satisfy IRCC.
mapped_rule: Quebec Applicants Need Certificat d'acceptation du Québec (CAQ)
error_message: Your CAQ must include Quebec's required attestation and allocation confirmation. An incomplete CAQ will not satisfy IRCC.

question: Do you have an education/employment gap longer than 12 months since Matric/FSc/A-Levels/Bachelors?
help_text: Gaps are common in Pakistan (exam delays, work, family). A gap alone is fine — an UNEXPLAINED gap is the problem. Routes to the next question.
mapped_rule: Educational Consistency and Study-Plan Logic (Bona Fide-linked)
error_message: An education or employment gap of over 12 months must be explained and evidenced in your application. An unexplained gap is a bona fide student risk factor.

question: If you have a 12+ month gap, can you justify it with evidence (job letters, transcripts, valid reasons)?
help_text: Provide employment letters, salary slips, freelance/contract proof, or transcripts covering the gap. Unevidenced 'I was preparing/at home' is weak and invites refusal.
mapped_rule: Educational Consistency and Study-Plan Logic (Bona Fide-linked)
error_message: An unexplained gap of over 12 months weakens your bona fide case. Provide employment letters, salary slips, freelance contracts, or transcripts covering the gap period.

question: Is your Canadian program in a substantially different field from your last qualification?
help_text: Allowed, but a large switch is scrutinised for genuineness. If yes, your Letter of Explanation must connect old and new fields with a credible career story.
mapped_rule: Educational Consistency and Study-Plan Logic (Bona Fide-linked)
error_message: A significant unexplained field switch is a bona fide refusal trigger. Your Letter of Explanation must connect your previous qualification to this program with a credible career narrative.

question: Are your transcripts/degrees verifiable and attested where needed (HEC/IBCC) with certified translations?
help_text: Provide HEC-attested degrees and IBCC-attested FSc/Matric where applicable, plus certified English translations. Unverifiable academics are a refusal/misrepresentation risk.
mapped_rule: Educational Consistency and Study-Plan Logic (Bona Fide-linked)
error_message: Inconsistent or unverifiable academic records raise fraud concerns. Provide HEC-attested degrees and IBCC-attested Matric/FSc results with certified English translations.

question: What is your first-year tuition (in CAD), per your LOA?
help_text: Enter the CAD tuition from your LOA. The tool adds living costs (CAD 22,895) and transport to compute required funds.
mapped_rule: Sufficient Financial Proof Required — Updated Threshold September 2025
error_message: Enter your first-year tuition amount in CAD as shown on your LOA. This is used to calculate the total funds required for your application.

question: How much do you have available for living costs (in CAD), excluding tuition/transport?
help_text: Outside Quebec, a single applicant must show CAD 22,895 for living costs (from Sept 2025), separate from tuition and travel. More for dependants; Quebec is higher.
mapped_rule: Sufficient Financial Proof Required — Updated Threshold September 2025
error_message: Outside Quebec, a single applicant must show CAD 22,895 for living costs (from September 2025), separate from tuition and return transport. Insufficient funds is a top refusal cause.

question: What is your TOTAL available funding (in CAD): living + first-year tuition + return transport?
help_text: Total must cover CAD 22,895 living + first-year tuition + ~CAD 1,500 return transport (plus dependants). Funds must be genuine and accessible, not a paper figure.
mapped_rule: Sufficient Financial Proof Required — Updated Threshold September 2025
error_message: Your total evidence must cover living costs plus first-year tuition plus return transport (~CAD 1,500). Funds must be genuine, accessible, and consistently held.

question: Do you have at least 4 months of bank statements showing a consistent balance?
help_text: IRCC expects ~4 months of statement history, not a fresh lump sum. A balance that appears suddenly before applying signals arranged funds.
mapped_rule: Sufficient Financial Proof Required — Updated Threshold September 2025
error_message: IRCC expects approximately 4 months of statement history showing a consistent balance. A lump sum appearing shortly before application is treated as arranged funds.

question: Has the money been held steadily (no sudden large jump just before applying)?
help_text: Consistency beats a recent injection. Erratic statements trigger doubts about whether funds are genuinely yours/accessible.
mapped_rule: Sufficient Financial Proof Required — Updated Threshold September 2025
error_message: Erratic or suddenly inflated balances raise doubts about whether funds are genuinely yours. Consistent statement history over several months is far stronger evidence.

question: What is the MAIN source of your funds?
help_text: Each source needs its own paper trail. Follow-up questions check whether that trail is documented.
mapped_rule: Sufficient Financial Proof Required — Updated Threshold September 2025
error_message: Each funding source requires its own documentary trail. Select all that apply — follow-up questions check whether each source is properly documented.

question: Were there any large/sudden deposits in the last few months?
help_text: Large deposits are not banned — but each must be explainable with a paper trail. Routes to the source-of-funds check.
mapped_rule: Sufficient Financial Proof Required — Updated Threshold September 2025
error_message: Large recent deposits are not banned but each must be explainable with a traceable paper trail: a sale deed, salary record, loan letter, or notarised gift affidavit.

question: Can you document the source of every significant deposit (sale deed, salary, loan letter, gift affidavit)?
help_text: The core legitimacy test. Each major deposit needs proof: registered sale deed for property, FBR-declared salary, sanctioned loan letter, or a notarised gift affidavit from a traceable giver.
mapped_rule: Sufficient Financial Proof Required — Updated Threshold September 2025
error_message: Every significant deposit must be proved with documentary evidence: a registered sale deed, FBR-declared salary, formal bank loan letter, or a notarised gift affidavit from a traceable source.

question: If sponsored, is your sponsor an immediate family member (parent, spouse, sibling)?
help_text: Immediate-family sponsorship is expected and trusted. Distant relatives or 'family friends' as sponsors raise scrutiny and need a strong relationship + funds explanation.
mapped_rule: Sufficient Financial Proof Required — Updated Threshold September 2025
error_message: Distant-relative or 'family friend' sponsors attract greater scrutiny. An immediate-family sponsor (parent, spouse, sibling) is expected and easier to establish.

question: If sponsored, does your sponsor file FBR tax returns consistent with the funds they are providing?
help_text: A sponsor showing large funds but no FBR tax history is a major red flag — it implies undeclared/untraceable income. Declared income should plausibly support the amount.
mapped_rule: Sufficient Financial Proof Required — Updated Threshold September 2025
error_message: A sponsor with large funds but no FBR filing history implies undeclared income. The sponsor's declared income should plausibly match the amount they are providing.

question: If property sale funds you, do you have the registered sale deed and bank-routed proceeds?
help_text: Property-sale funding is fine if the deed is registered and proceeds entered the account via banking channel — not cash.
mapped_rule: Sufficient Financial Proof Required — Updated Threshold September 2025
error_message: Property-sale proceeds are accepted if the sale deed is registered and the proceeds were routed through a banking channel — not received as cash.

question: If a loan funds you, do you have an official sanction/disbursement letter from a recognised bank?
help_text: Education loans are accepted with a formal sanction letter from a recognised institution. Informal/family loans carry less weight.
mapped_rule: Sufficient Financial Proof Required — Updated Threshold September 2025
error_message: An education loan requires a formal sanction letter from a recognised bank. Informal family loans carry significantly less weight as financial evidence.

question: Do you have funds for return transportation (~CAD 1,500)?
help_text: Return travel cost must be covered on top of living + tuition.
mapped_rule: Sufficient Financial Proof Required — Updated Threshold September 2025
error_message: Return transportation cost (~CAD 1,500) must be evidenced on top of living costs and tuition. It is a required component of total funds.

question: Do you have (or plan to buy) a GIC from a participating Canadian bank?
help_text: SDS ended (Nov 2024) so a GIC is no longer mandatory, but it is still accepted and strengthens financial proof. Routes the next questions.
mapped_rule: Guaranteed Investment Certificate (GIC) Still Accepted as Financial Evidence
error_message: A GIC from a participating bank is still accepted as financial evidence, though it is no longer mandatory since SDS closed. It must be accompanied by separate tuition and transport evidence.

question: If using a GIC, is it from a participating bank (CIBC, BMO, Scotiabank, RBC, TD, National Bank)?
help_text: Only GICs from participating institutions are recognised. Verify before buying.
mapped_rule: Guaranteed Investment Certificate (GIC) Still Accepted as Financial Evidence
error_message: Only GICs from IRCC-recognised institutions (CIBC, BMO, Scotiabank, RBC, TD, National Bank) are accepted. A GIC from another institution will not count.

question: Do you understand a GIC alone is not enough — tuition and transport must also be evidenced?
help_text: A GIC covers part of living costs; you must still evidence tuition payment and transport separately.
mapped_rule: Guaranteed Investment Certificate (GIC) Still Accepted as Financial Evidence
error_message: A GIC covers part of your living costs but does not replace tuition or return transport evidence. All three elements must be evidenced separately.

question: Will you be in Canada for 6 months or more?
help_text: Stays of 6+ months generally require an immigration medical exam (IME). Routes the medical questions.
mapped_rule: Medical Exam Required for Stays of 6+ Months
error_message: Most study permit holders stay more than 6 months. This determines whether an immigration medical exam (IME) is required for your application.

question: If required, have you completed your immigration medical exam (IME)?
help_text: An IME is required for 6+ month stays. Pakistani applicants typically need TB screening (chest X-ray).
mapped_rule: Medical Exam Required for Stays of 6+ Months
error_message: An immigration medical exam by an IRCC panel physician is required for stays of 6 months or more. Pakistani applicants typically require TB screening.

question: Will you use an IRCC-approved panel physician (not a random local clinic)?
help_text: Only exams by IRCC panel physicians count. A cheaper local clinic's report is worthless for the permit.
mapped_rule: Medical Exam Required for Stays of 6+ Months
error_message: Only exams conducted by IRCC-approved panel physicians are accepted. A report from a local clinic not on the panel list is worthless for the study permit application.

question: Have you paid (or will you pay) the biometrics fee?
help_text: Biometrics (CAD ~85) apply to most applicants aged 14–79. Pay it and book at a VAC in Pakistan.
mapped_rule: Biometrics Required for Most Applicants Aged 14–79
error_message: The biometrics fee (~CAD 85) must be paid as part of your application. Biometrics are required for most applicants aged 14–79 and are given at a Visa Application Centre.

question: Have you completed biometrics at a Visa Application Centre?
help_text: Complete biometrics at a VAC after receiving the Biometrics Instruction Letter (BIL). Delays here slow processing.
mapped_rule: Biometrics Required for Most Applicants Aged 14–79
error_message: Biometrics must be completed at a VAC in Pakistan after you receive your Biometrics Instruction Letter. Delays in completing biometrics slow application processing.

question: Do you have your Biometrics Instruction Letter (BIL)?
help_text: The BIL is issued after you apply and pay; you need it to give biometrics.
mapped_rule: Biometrics Required for Most Applicants Aged 14–79
error_message: Your Biometrics Instruction Letter is issued by IRCC after you submit and pay. You need it before you can give biometrics at a VAC.

question: Have you EVER had a visa refusal, cancellation, or overstay in ANY country (UK, USA, Canada, Schengen, etc.)?
help_text: Prior refusals are visible and heavily weighed. A refusal is survivable IF disclosed and explained — concealment is fatal and is misrepresentation.
mapped_rule: Immigration History and Full Disclosure
error_message: Prior refusals, cancellations, or overstays in any country are visible to IRCC. They must be disclosed — concealment is misrepresentation with a 5-year A40 bar.

question: If yes, which country/countries and the stated reason?
help_text: Note each refusal and reason — you must address each in your Letter of Explanation.
mapped_rule: Immigration History and Full Disclosure
error_message: Record each prior refusal, its country, and the stated reason accurately. You must address each one in your Letter of Explanation.

question: Have you ever claimed asylum/protection in any country?
help_text: An asylum history strongly conflicts with 'temporary student who will leave' and must be addressed candidly, ideally with legal advice.
mapped_rule: Immigration History and Full Disclosure
error_message: A prior asylum claim strongly conflicts with temporary student intent and must be disclosed honestly in your application, ideally with qualified legal advice.

question: Are ALL your documents and statements completely truthful, with nothing omitted or altered?
help_text: Misrepresentation (fake bank balances, altered transcripts, hidden refusals) causes refusal AND a 5-year ban under A40. This applies even if an agent did it in your name.
mapped_rule: All Documents and Statements Must Be Truthful (Misrepresentation Bar)
error_message: Any misrepresentation — fake bank balances, altered transcripts, hidden refusals — triggers refusal and a 5-year inadmissibility bar under A40, even if an agent prepared the documents.

question: Do you understand the Student Direct Stream (SDS) has ended and you apply via the regular stream?
help_text: SDS ended 8 Nov 2024. There is no fast GIC+IELTS shortcut now — everyone uses the regular study permit stream.
mapped_rule: Student Direct Stream (SDS) Ended — November 8, 2024
error_message: The Student Direct Stream ended on 8 November 2024. All applicants now use the regular study permit stream; there is no fast-track GIC+IELTS shortcut.

question: Do you plan to change DLI after arriving?
help_text: Since Nov 2024 you must apply for a NEW study permit to change DLI — you cannot just switch. Routes the next question.
mapped_rule: Changing Schools Requires a New Study Permit (From November 8, 2024)
error_message: Indicate whether you plan to change DLI after arriving. Since November 2024, changing DLI requires an approved new study permit before switching.

question: Do you understand a school change now needs a new study permit (approved before switching)?
help_text: Switching DLI without a new permit breaches your conditions. Plan your program carefully before applying.
mapped_rule: Changing Schools Requires a New Study Permit (From November 8, 2024)
error_message: Switching DLI without an approved new study permit breaches your conditions of stay. You must apply for and receive the new permit before changing institutions.

question: Do you understand you can only work off-campus once your program has started?
help_text: Off-campus work is only allowed after studies begin, not on arrival.
mapped_rule: Off-Campus Work Limited to 24 Hours Per Week
error_message: Off-campus work is only permitted after your studies have begun — not from the date of arrival. Understand this timing before travelling to Canada.

question: Do you understand the 24-hours-per-week off-campus work limit during sessions?
help_text: Off-campus work is capped at 24 hrs/week while classes are in session (full-time during scheduled breaks). Over-working breaches your permit.
mapped_rule: Off-Campus Work Limited to 24 Hours Per Week
error_message: Off-campus work is limited to 24 hours per week while classes are in session. Exceeding this limit breaches your study permit conditions.

question: Do you know you need a SIN to work in Canada?
help_text: A Social Insurance Number is required to work legally; apply after arrival.
mapped_rule: Off-Campus Work Limited to 24 Hours Per Week
error_message: A Social Insurance Number is required to work legally in Canada. Apply for one after arriving — bring your study permit and other identity documents.

question: Do you understand authorized leave from studies cannot exceed 150 days?
help_text: Stopping studies beyond 150 days without authorisation can lead to loss of status.
mapped_rule: Authorized Leave Cannot Exceed 150 Days
error_message: Pausing studies beyond 150 days without authorisation risks loss of your study permit status. Understand this requirement before travelling to Canada.

question: Do you understand you must apply to extend BEFORE your permit expires?
help_text: Apply to extend at least 30 days before expiry to keep maintained status.
mapped_rule: Must Apply to Extend Study Permit Before It Expires
error_message: You must apply to extend your study permit before it expires to maintain your legal status in Canada. Apply at least 30 days before expiry.

question: Are you bringing a spouse/common-law partner who wants to work?
help_text: Spousal open work permits are now restricted (see next question). Routes accordingly.
mapped_rule: Spousal Open Work Permit Now Restricted to Masters (16+ Months) and Doctoral Students
error_message: Indicate whether you are bringing a spouse or common-law partner who wishes to work. Spousal open work permits are now restricted to specific program types.

question: If yes, is your program Masters (16+ months)/doctoral or another OWP-eligible program?
help_text: From Jan 2025, spousal OWPs are limited mainly to spouses of Masters (16+ months)/doctoral and select students. Undergrad/college spouses are generally ineligible.
mapped_rule: Spousal Open Work Permit Now Restricted to Masters (16+ Months) and Doctoral Students
error_message: From January 2025, spousal open work permits are mainly limited to spouses of Masters (16+ months) or doctoral students. Undergraduate or short-program spouses are generally ineligible.

question: Is a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) part of your plan?
help_text: PGWP eligibility now depends on the DLI AND, for non-degree programs, the field of study. Routes the next questions.
mapped_rule: PGWP Requires PGWP-Eligible DLI and Qualifying Field of Study (Non-Degree Programs)
error_message: Indicate whether a Post-Graduation Work Permit is part of your plan. PGWP eligibility depends on both the DLI and, for non-degree programs, the field of study.

question: If aiming for PGWP, is your DLI/program PGWP-eligible?
help_text: Confirm PGWP eligibility before enrolling. Some programs/DLIs do not qualify — a common trap sold by agents.
mapped_rule: PGWP Requires PGWP-Eligible DLI and Qualifying Field of Study (Non-Degree Programs)
error_message: Not all DLIs or programs qualify for a PGWP. Confirm your DLI and program are PGWP-eligible before enrolling — agents commonly sell PGWP-ineligible programs.

question: For a non-degree program, have you checked it maps to an eligible field (CIP) for PGWP?
help_text: Non-degree (college diploma) PGWP eligibility is now tied to fields linked to labour shortages. Verify your program's field.
mapped_rule: PGWP Requires PGWP-Eligible DLI and Qualifying Field of Study (Non-Degree Programs)
error_message: For non-degree programs, PGWP eligibility depends on the Classification of Instructional Programs (CIP) code. Verify your program maps to an eligible field before enrolling.

question: Did an education agent/consultant prepare or submit any of your documents?
help_text: Using an agent is fine — but YOU are responsible for everything submitted in your name. Routes to verification.
mapped_rule: Application Integrity and Agent Risk
error_message: Using an education agent is permitted, but you are legally responsible for everything submitted in your name regardless of who prepared it.

question: Have you personally read and verified EVERY document and answer submitted in your name?
help_text: Some agents inflate bank balances, fake experience letters, or alter transcripts. If an agent fabricated anything, YOU face refusal AND a 5-year misrepresentation ban (A40). Verify every line yourself.
mapped_rule: Application Integrity and Agent Risk
error_message: You must personally verify every document and answer submitted in your name. Agent-fabricated content — false balances, altered transcripts — makes you liable for refusal and a 5-year ban.

question: Is your agent reputable/authorised (institution-linked or a regulated consultant), not an unknown middleman?
help_text: Prefer institution-authorised reps or an ICCRC/CICC-regulated consultant. 'Guaranteed visa' middlemen cause most fraud-related refusals.
mapped_rule: Application Integrity and Agent Risk
error_message: Use a reputable, institution-authorised agent or an ICCRC/CICC-regulated consultant. Unregulated 'guaranteed visa' middlemen are the primary source of fraud-related refusals.
